title: Concurrent agents share a working tree and a git index with no coordination protocol
problem: Two agents, or an agent and me, wrote to the same repository at the same time, and one of them committed or reverted the other's work without either noticing.
symptom: Unrelated edits appear inside a loop's commit, or uncommitted work vanishes after a failure-path reset; nobody's log shows an error.
why_now: Agent frameworks assume a single writer per repository. The git index is process-shared, so blanket staging and reset-to-remote are destructive to a co-writer, and there is no standard sentinel or lease that a second writer must respect.
existing: Path-limited commits: protect the loop from a human, not the human from the loop, and cannot stage untracked files.
Worktrees or clones per agent: correct but unadopted, and merge remains unspecified.
Ad-hoc STOP files: effective, but every team invents its own semantics.

evidence.title: INC-0012: a loop's git add -A sweeps a human's uncommitted edits into its commit
evidence.quote: The git index is process-shared. A blanket `git add -A` stages everything in the tree, including uncommitted work you did not author.

evidence.title: INC-0014: a revert-on-failure loop destroys uncommitted human work
evidence.quote: A loop's revert-to-remote cannot distinguish loop dirt from human work-in-progress.
evidence.note: Classified critical. The recorded mitigation is a per-team sentinel naming owner, files at risk, lift condition and whether a restart is needed - i.e. a convention, not a runtime guarantee.

build_hypothesis: A lease file with a declared owner, scope of paths and expiry that both loop and human tooling check before staging or resetting, plus a merge rule for the case where the lease is stale.
